title: Introduce randomized-primer-cascade-runner and ordinal-variance reporter
author: Riley Chen
description:
Motivation: We need a lightweight, stochastic workload generator that stresses KV cache transitions and session fragmentation without coupling to existing traffic replayers. This PR adds a randomized primer-cascade runner (a compact runner that composes short primer sequences into cascades with controlled overlap and randomness) and an ordinal-variance reporter (a reporter that computes ordinal statistics across repeated epochal runs and emits a compact 'flame-diff' highlighting kernel/line-level variance).

What it does: The primer-cascade-runner synthesizes cascades of short primer sequences to provoke cache churn, KV cache eviction, and sequence boundary effects in the serving runtime. It supports configuration for cascade depth, primer pool entropy, overlap probability, and per-step token distributions. The ordinal-variance reporter runs N repeated epochs, aligns token-level trace points across runs by event ordinal (not wall-clock), and computes variance metrics per kernel and per source line. The reporter outputs: 1) an aggregated ordinal-variance JSON, 2) a guided flame-diff SVG that highlights regions exceeding configured variance thresholds, and 3) a compact CSV suitable for automated alerts.

Key design points: - Stochastic primers are seeded deterministically by run id to allow reproducible failure cases while preserving randomness across seeds. - Ordinal alignment avoids time-sync noise and surfaces algorithmic instability (e.g., non-deterministic scheduling or micro-batching artifacts). - The runner is intentionally lightweight (single-process, low-memory) so it can be run in CI perf lanes and on small perf clusters.

Backward compatibility: Runner and reporter are additive and do not modify existing harness interfaces. Existing replayers remain unchanged. The new CLI flags are namespaced under 'primer-cascade' and 'ordinal-variance' to minimize collisions.

How to run locally: ./benchmarks/run_bench.sh --runner primer-cascade --seed 42 --cascade-depth 8 --overlap-prob 0.15 --epochs 20 --reporter ordinal-variance --variance-threshold 0.12

Outputs & example metrics: In a 20-epoch run against the baseline Llama-7B micro-config, we observed per-kernel ordinal variance spikes localized to the KV slab allocator and attention softmax kernel; the guided flame-diff highlighted a 37% ordinal-variance increase at P95 for the attention softmax under high primer entropy.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for primer generation, seed determinism and ordinal alignment. - Integration test that runs a 3-epoch job in CI perf lane and asserts reporter artifacts are produced. - Added synthetic golden traces used by ordinal-variance to validate alignment logic.

Docs: Added a README at docs/benchmarks/primer_cascade.md with configuration examples, interpretation guidance for the ordinal-variance report, and sample artifacts.

Related work: This complements the existing replay-based runners by targeting cache-transition pathology and algorithmic instability detection. Linked Linear tickets: ENG-8271 (primer-cascade) and PM-294 (reporting requirements).

review_comments: Jasper O'Neill: Nice focused addition. A couple of asks: 1) can the runner emit an optional token-level map for KV hits so we can cross-reference with the profiler? 2) please add a small example output artifact to the docs directory.
Riley Chen: Reply: added optional --emit-token-map flag and included a 3-epoch example in docs artifacts. See commit a8c9b21.
Maya Patel: Request changes: The SVG flame-diff generation should not rely on lxml (native stdlib preferred). Also please guard heavy ops behind a --no-render flag for CI.
Riley Chen: Reply: replaced lxml usage with a tiny svg builder in svg_flame_diff.py and added --no-render for CI. Updated tests to skip rendering in CI lanes.
Lukas Schneider: Approved after minor nits. Suggestion: consider exposing an API hook for the console to fetch the CSV for dashboard ingestion.
ci_checks: integration-tests: passed (id: it-3341) - runs a 3-epoch smoke against a micro-config
perf-regression-check: passed (id: perf-1103) - compares ordinal-variance baseline and asserts no regression above threshold
merge_summary: Merged via squash on 2026-02-13 by Maya Patel. Merge commit: 5f3b2a4. Notes: kept detailed commits in PR description; docs and CI pipeline added. No breaking changes. The reporter artifacts sit under benchmark-artifacts/{run-id}/ordinal-variance/ for downstream pipelines.
release_notes: Add new primer-cascade workload runner to exercise KV cache transitions and an ordinal-variance reporter that generates variance JSON, guided flame-diff SVG, and CSV exports. Useful for catching algorithmic instability and micro-batching artifacts.
notes_for_ops: CI perf lane now includes a short 3-epoch run using this runner; long runs should be scheduled off-hours. Reporter produces SVGs that can be large; use --no-render in CI to avoid flakiness. Artifacts are uploaded to s3://redwood-benchmarks/primer-cascade/{run-id}/
impact_summary: Low-risk additive benchmark tooling. Helps detect non-deterministic behavior and kernel-level variance spikes. Expected to improve our ability to triage intermittent perf regressions and provide clearer diff artifacts for perf reviews.
